subject: Post-demo follow-up: hosted API budget anchor + peak surge profile
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa@cloudscribe.com>, Marcus Reed <m.reed@cloudscribe.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: hosted API budget anchor + peak surge profile

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the practical walkthrough of the CloudScribe use case. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a concrete hosted pricing proposal and Mutual Action Plan.

TL;DR from our side:
- Expected monthly token volume range (you mentioned): ~75M–120M tokens. Please confirm if that’s steady-state or includes the new feature launch in Q4.
- Avg tokens per end-user request (ballpark): you said ~1.2k tokens (prompt + response). If that changes by >20% we should re-run the unit-econ.
- Peak concurrency/99th TPS: you called out spikes during marketing campaigns — target 99th percentile ~260 TPS, momentary peaks up to ~320 for 3–6 minutes.
- Budget target: you mentioned a $/1M token target in the $400–$500 range (I heard $450 as a midpoint).

What we’ll do next (in parallel):
1) I’ll run unit-econ scenarios against three committed slab options (monthly commit bands + burst buckets) and share the math. Expect: committed 50M / 100M / 200M bands with blended $/1M options.
2) Ops (Karthik) will validate the 99th/peak TPS profile and confirm whether hosted can absorb the short bursts vs suggesting Dedicated burst capacity.
3) We’ll prepare a short SOW + timeline for a 30-day pilot (instrumentation + cost telemetry) to validate the traffic shape in production.

Action for you: please confirm two numbers so our pricing calc is accurate — (a) final monthly token target you want to commit to (pick a single number inside the 75–120M range), and (b) average tokens per request (if different from 1,200). Attaching the traffic estimate sheet you shared (CloudScribe_traffic_estimates.xlsx) — we’ll use that as the source of truth once you confirm.

If procurement wants a template SOW or a quick checklist for vendor onboarding, we can include that in the packet.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415 555 0128
attachments: CloudScribe_traffic_estimates.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alyssa King <alyssa@cloudscribe.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <m.reed@cloudscribe.com>, procurement@cloudscribe.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: hosted API budget anchor + peak surge profile

Thanks Dylan — great session. Quick answers below and a small clarification on the traffic shape.

Confirmed numbers:
- Committed monthly target we’d prefer to anchor on: 90,000,000 tokens / month (this is our conservative mid-point for Q4 ramp).
- Avg tokens per request: 1,200 (includes ~400 tokens of system prompt + 800 tokens returned on average).
- Peak: 99th percentile ~260 TPS; we’ve observed campaign-driven microbursts to ~320 TPS lasting 3–7 minutes.
- Budget ceiling we can tolerate for vendor cost: $/1M target ~ $450; stretch up to $525 if latency/SLOs are nailed.

Procurement note (procurement@cloudscribe.com): we’ll need an initial 30-day pilot SOW and a list of SOC2 artifacts. Marcus — looping you for procurement timing; we aim to have vendor in place by end of September.

I attached a short SOW outline we typically push to vendors (SOW_outline.pdf) — use it if helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk through the numbers live.

Best,
Alyssa King
Head of Platform, CloudScribe
attachments: CloudScribe_SOW_outline.pdf (pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa@cloudscribe.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: hosted API budget anchor + peak surge profile

Perfect — thanks for the confirmation, Alyssa. I’ll turn this into a concrete pricing packet and a two-option pilot plan. A few quick notes I’ll include in the packet so we’re aligned:

Unit-econ assumptions I’ll use (unless you flag changes):
- Monthly commit: 90M tokens.
- Avg tokens/request: 1,200 -> implies ~75k to 95k requests/day depending on weekly profiles.
- Blended target $/1M tokens: $450 (you indicated this as target ceiling).
- Expected monthly cost at $450/1M = (90 * $450) = $40,500/month vendor cost baseline (we’ll show incremental lower tiers for higher commits).

Pilot proposal (two tracks):
A) Short pilot — 30 days on Hosted API with instrumentation, token-level telemetry, and a burst buffer. Objective: validate 99th TPS and observe real-world tokens/request distribution.
B) Pilot + Dedicated readiness — same telemetry but add reserved burst capacity and a canary rollback plan (for heavy marketing spikes).

Ops asks (Karthik) — please validate the 320 TPS short-burst feasibility on Hosted. If we need Dedicated burst to keep 99th p90 latency < 250ms, flag that and provide an estimated incremental cost for a 1-week burst reserve.

Marissa — I’ll share the draft pricing packet and SOW in the next 24 hours for your review (also including the SOC2 artifact list Alyssa requested).

Next steps: I’ll send a follow-up with the three slab math and two pilot options by EOD tomorrow. If procurement wants the SOW in DocuSign, let me know the procurement contact name and I’ll route it.

Thanks all,
Dylan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa King <alyssa@cloudscribe.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: hosted API budget anchor + peak surge profile

Quick ops readout — digging into infra sizing and short-burst handling.

Summary: Hosted can absorb sustained 99th of ~260 TPS with our autoscaling profile, but repeated microbursts to ~320 TPS for 5–7 minutes will push us into higher queueing unless we do one of the following:
- Enable a burst buffer (hosted burst pool) for CloudScribe — low-friction, billable by peak throughput; or
- Recommend a small Dedicated burst reservation (single-week reserve during campaigns) to guarantee latency SLOs.

A couple of cost-control levers to call out (helps the $/1M target):
- Prefix/KV caching for common user prompts — for CloudScribe we estimate ~8–12% token reduction on repeated prompts during campaigns.
- Response-length caps on marketing flows (trim tail tokens) — small UX tradeoff that can drop average tokens/request by ~10%.

Preliminary pricing guidance for the packet (we’ll finalize math before sending):
- 50M commit: $520 / 1M (no burst)
- 100M commit: $460 / 1M (includes moderate burst buffer)
- 200M commit: $380 / 1M (best unit-econ + preferred for heavy growth)

If Alyssa confirms 90M commit we can offer an effective blended $/1M around $440 with a managed burst buffer and SOC2 artifacts included in the pilot.

Action: Dylan/Marissa to produce the packet; Ops to include a short note on burst options and a one-week Dedicated reserve cost if they want guaranteed latency for campaign windows.

Karthik
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
